post_letter_observations: No adjustment records. Every letter pointer was followed into the revised manuscript. No pointer located evidence that 2A missed, no rebuttal refutes a 2A finding on the merits, and no 2A reading mistook an item's target. Final verdicts therefore equal Phase 2A verdicts for all 38 items. The three dissents (DIS-1 R1, DIS-2 R5, DIS-3 R13) are untouched and await adjudication.

R3 rebuttal considered and rejected as valid_rebuttal: the letter argues that response curves make an early-window calibration unnecessary. The curves plot outcomes against the realised pass rate, which is the same endogenous quantity the round-1 concern targets, so they do not stand in for an outcome-independent calibration.

R15: the letter says 'most' of the corner's effect comes from shifting distrustful agents; the manuscript says 'part ... and the rest'. Table 2 supports 'most' for cosine (124 -> 107 by level shift, -> 78 by corner, so about 17 of 46 points come from the mean shift). The manuscript could state this split numerically. This is not counted as an overstatement.

S17: the letter answers the bias question ('trust shrinks perceived policy and bias together') only in the letter. Adding one sentence to §6.1 saying whether this is intended would close half the item.

R1: the letter and the closing statement say the missing survey is 'named as a limitation of scope'. Adding that sentence, plus an explicit pre-emptive-guideline framing, to §8 and §1 would match the letter and address option (b).

Letter details absent from the manuscript (response-curve grid of 6 spaces x 3 metrics x 10 coverages, 7,200 crossing runs, CITATION.cff, golden tests) should move into the ODD, Appendix B or Code and data. This overlaps frozen NEW-3 and adds no new issue.

Commitment axis (decision-inert): C4 and C5 were triaged will_address. The letter delivers C4 partially (4,000 rather than 8,000 rounds). For C5 it claims a cost note that cannot be found in the manuscript.

The letter's section numbering (§4 matching, §5 ruler, §6 case, §7 audit list) matches the revised manuscript. Its table numbering does not: it calls the interaction tables 'Tables 3-4', but they are Tables 2-3 in float order.

new_issues.description: Interaction estimand undefined and not reconciled with the lag index. The paper's main case claim rests on 'Euclidean's lag contrast in the relative shock effect minus cosine's', but 'relative shock effect' is never defined, and the interaction and the index disagree in ordering in some cells without comment: centred/run/anchor/own-opinion gives indices Euclidean 134 [129,139] < cosine 150 [145,154] (by the index, cosine amplifies more) yet interaction +0.001 [-0.004,+0.007]; unit/run/anchor/centre gives 189 vs 187 yet interaction +0.020 [+0.014,+0.027]. Readers cannot tell which estimand carries 'which geometry amplified the lag effect more'.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §5.2 Design last para, 'the paired interaction: Euclidean's lag contrast in the relative shock effect minus cosine's'
new_issues.competence_basis: Simulation-methods seat: estimand definition and consistency of paired contrasts vs ratio indices.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Original §5.2 l.209 already reported 'the paired lag contrast in the relative shock effect ... and its difference between geometries' without definition, and original Table 2 already showed unit/matched-run/anchor 189 vs 187 with +0.020; the revision adds the own-target instance (Table 3) but the underlying defect is present in both versions.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: S17 asks for the interaction's sign convention and the bias-shrinkage question; S10 asks for absolute effects next to the ratio. Neither asks for the interaction's estimand to be defined or reconciled with the index where they disagree in ordering.

new_issues.description: Fig. 4 row labels and caption do not map consistently onto the text. Caption says the fixes (cos, rng, split) are 'applied (1) or not (0)', but rows are labelled split=30/40. Measured from the figure, the text's 'draft's own engine and settings' interaction (+0.034 [+0.025,+0.044]) matches the cos=0 rng=0 split=30 row (~+0.034 [+0.024,+0.044]) and the 'all other fixes' value (+0.029 [+0.020,+0.039]) matches cos=1 rng=1 split=40, while the trust-only variant of the draft (+0.026 [+0.013,+0.038]) sits on cos=0 rng=0 split=40 and the all-fixes+trust row on split=30. No single reading of 'split' makes all four consistent.
new_issues.location_anchor: figure: Fig. 4, pre-audit rows and caption 'applied (1) or not (0)'
new_issues.competence_basis: Pixel-measured dot and CI positions in fig4_interaction_all_cells.png calibrated on two known rows (+0.034 and -0.057), checked against numbers.tex macros.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Fig. 4, its caption and the VCDraft*/VCDraftFixed* macros are new in the revision (original had a bar chart of forward indices, fig3_case_factorial, and no backward-row figure).
new_issues.non_match_rationale: R4 required the interaction to be reported for every cell, which it now is; this is a labelling/identity error inside the new display, not a gap in coverage or quantification.

new_issues.description: The response-curve experiment that the abstract offers as the paper's answer ('we report whole response curves instead') is undocumented: the threshold grid, seeds (50, apparently separate from the factorial's 100), horizon and how the realised pass rate is computed appear nowhere in §4.1 or the ODD, and the curves carry no uncertainty bands.
new_issues.location_anchor: figure: Fig. 2 caption, 'as the threshold varies. One line per metric, each point the mean of 50 seeds'
new_issues.competence_basis: Simulation-methods seat: reproducibility of design and uncertainty reporting.
